issues.body: The new header says `data.ttl.tgz` is fixed because every accepted upload now carries a suffix-stripped/inner `effectiveName`. On the real path, `decompressDatasetBytes` treats `tgz` as gzip but `innerNameForSource` intentionally returns `null` for that extension. `maybeDecompressBytes` then uses the original `data.ttl.tgz`, and `guessFormat` does not strip `.tgz`, so it still selects Turtle by fallback. More importantly, gzip decoding a `.tgz` yields tar bytes, not the RDF member text, so such an upload cannot be correctly parsed merely by propagating a name. This makes the stated scope incorrect and leaves an explicitly named regression unfixed and untested.
issues.fix_hint: Either implement actual tar-member extraction and return that member's name, with a non-vacuous `.tgz` browser test, or remove `.tgz`/`data.ttl.tgz` from the supported and fixed claims (and reject tar-gzip clearly rather than accepting it as RDF text). Keep the ZIP `effectiveName` behavior and its existing regression test.
issues.title: The claimed `.tgz` fix is not implemented by the effective-name propagation

verdict.summary: The ZIP inner-member fix and its N-Quads regression test are sound, but the change overclaims and does not handle one of the explicitly cited cases. For `.tgz`, the decompressor deliberately returns no inner name, so `effectiveName` falls back to the outer `.tgz` name and format detection still falls back to Turtle; moreover the decoded payload remains a tar stream rather than the member RDF text. The new comments therefore describe behavior the real path does not provide.
